title: Customer and Wallet Due Diligence
summary: How to onboard and keep under review customers whose activity involves crypto-assets, including source of funds and wealth, ownership of self-hosted wallets and risk-based enhanced due diligence.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to onboard and keep under review customers whose activity involves crypto-assets, including source of funds and wealth, ownership of self-hosted wallets and risk-based enhanced due diligence.
Learning Objectives: Design a customer risk assessment that reflects crypto-asset activity
Verify source of funds and wealth derived from crypto-assets
Apply proportionate controls to self-hosted wallets and peer-to-peer transfers
Syllabus: Customer risk factors for crypto-asset activity and business customers
Source of funds and wealth: using on-chain history as evidence
Self-hosted wallets: proof of ownership, risk scoring and limits
Enhanced due diligence, periodic review and trigger events
Intended Audience: MLROs, compliance officers and financial crime analysts at crypto-asset service providers
Financial crime teams at payment, e-money and fintech firms with crypto-asset exposure or crypto-asset business customers
Product, operations and risk managers responsible for onboarding, wallets, withdrawals and monitoring tools
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT compliance or financial crime operations is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Virtual Assets Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
